question: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Reference class first: 9-10 trading-day changes in DGS10 have a median of ~0 and no exploitable drift, so the prior is the last print carried forward (4.77-4.79 as of Sep 3-4 per FRED/H.15/TradingEconomics). Only 9 sessions elapse (Sep 7 is Labor Day), but the window is unusually event-dense: Aug CPI Sep 11 (Waller named it as decisive), a live FOMC Sep 16 with hike odds oscillating 50-65%, and an escalating US-Iran Hormuz conflict with Brent +7-8% on the week. Two-sided: oil passthrough, hawkish Warsh, +31bp of momentum since July and a 19-year-high 30Y push up; Waller/Williams dovishness, a mostly pre-priced hike, flight-to-quality on escalation, and buyers at a 3-year-high level push down. Neither side dominates, so the median stays at spot 4.79 with a small right skew for the term-premium tail. Dispersion is the real call: I widened past the calm-August realized (~6-13bp) but stayed under naive event-scaled iid (~17bp), landing at sigma 15.5bp. No Sep-18-matching prediction market exists; Kalshi's weekly 10Y book 429'd, and its year-end contracts (56% >=4.75, 27% >5.00) are a different horizon, treated as evidence only. 2% above 5.255 prices a hot-CPI-plus-hawkish-hike-plus-term-premium selloff (Oct 2023 precedent: +45bp in 9 sessions); no mechanism gets 130bp lower in 9 sessions, so no lower escape declared.

Fed H.15 / FRED DGS10 is the constant-maturity series; CNBC/TradingEconomics market quotes typically sit within 1-3bp of it.

EVIDENCE (source, date):
- Aug payrolls printed +162k vs +56k consensus, released Fri Sep 4; yields reversed two sessions of declines and rose ~3bp (TradingEconomics, Sep 4).
- Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said at Jackson Hole that underlying inflation had not 'meaningfully improved' and the Fed has 'work to do'; this shifted market pricing toward a September hike (CNBC, Aug 31).
- Fed Governor Waller said Sep 3 he would support holding rates if price pressures keep easing, and that his vote turns on the August inflation data; hike odds fell from ~63% to ~50% intraday, then rebounded to ~60-65% after payrolls (CNBC Sep 3; Haberler Sep 6; Marketplace Aug 31).
- NY Fed's Williams said inflation is slowing because energy prices are not passing through to services (Haberler, Sep 6).
- FOMC meets Sep 15-16, decision and statement Sep 16 - inside the window (CNBC / Chase, Aug-Sep 2026).
- August CPI is scheduled for Fri Sep 11, 8:30am ET; PPI is the same week - both inside the window (BLS release schedule / financecalendar.com).
- 2Y yield reached 4.42%, its highest since January 2025; 30Y index around 5.25% and topped 5.31% on Aug 17, a 19-year high (Haberler Sep 6; CNBC Aug 17; StockCharts).
- The 10Y touched 4.818% intraweek, described as the highest since November 2023 (CNBC, Sep 2).
- US struck an Iranian crude tanker (M/T Kylo) in the Gulf of Oman on Sep 5, following weekend exchanges of fire and two tankers hit leaving the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's chief negotiator said 'the era of proportionate responses is over' (CBC / CNBC Sep 1-5).
- Brent gained 7.2-8.6% and WTI over 9% in the week to Sep 4-5; US average diesel hit a record $5.85; European gas above EUR75/MWh (New Indian Express Sep 5; Haberler Sep 6).
- Sell-side year-end 2026 forecasts cited in the week's commentary cluster at 4.25%-4.50% for the 10Y (Nuveen/weekly-commentary roundup, early Sep 2026).
- Prediction markets on 10Y levels exist only at year-end horizons, not for Sep 18: Kalshi year-end brackets and Polymarket 'how high before 2027'. The Kalshi weekly series KXTNOTEW and daily KXUST10AD cover 10Y yield brackets but the Sep 18 book was not retrievable (HTTP 429).

BASE RATES / DISPERSION (with the class each is computed over):
- Over all trailing-12m 9-to-10-trading-day windows in DGS10: median change ~0, essentially no drift.
- Over August 2026 only (a calm month): daily change SD 4.3bp; overlapping 10-day changes SD ~5-6bp, range -6bp to +14bp.
- Over the 12 calendar months Sep 2025-Aug 2026, month-first to month-last changes: SD ~14bp; largest single-month moves -25bp (Feb 2026) and +27bp (Mar 2026, Jul 2026).
- Over the same 12 months, intra-month high-low range: mean ~22bp, min 12bp (Aug 2026), max 39bp (Mar 2026).
- Conditional on the window containing both a CPI print and an FOMC decision (the case here), event-day variance runs materially above the unconditional daily figure; naive iid scaling of the August daily SD to 9 sessions gives ~13bp, and substituting elevated variance for the two event days gives ~17bp.
- Level trajectory over the past year (DGS10 month-end): Sep 2025 4.20, Oct 4.11, Nov 4.02, Dec 4.18, Jan 2026 4.24, Feb 3.97, Mar 4.30, Apr 4.40, May 4.45, Jun 4.44, Jul 4.75, Aug 4.73. Trailing-12m low 3.97 (Feb 2026), high 4.79 (Sep 1-2, 2026).
- Event-in-window base rate for a >=45bp 9-session move: zero occurrences in the trailing 12 months of DGS10; the nearest precedent outside that window is Oct 2023 (4.57 -> 5.02 in ~9 sessions).

SEARCHED FOR BUT COULD NOT FIND: live prices on the Kalshi weekly 10Y yield book for the week ending Sep 18 (HTTP 429) or any Polymarket/Manifold contract matching this question's resolution date and instrument - the harness title search also returned none; the CNBC US10Y live quote page (HTTP 403); the September FOMC dot-plot expectations in any quantitative form; any published consensus forecast specific to the Sep 18 level; the Sep 4 H.15 value as a confirmed release rather than a vendor quote.
calls.reference_class: 9-to-10-trading-day changes in the US 10Y Treasury constant-maturity yield (DGS10), trailing 12 months, windows containing both a CPI print and an FOMC decision

calls.reasoning: Resolution is the 10Y level at the Sep 18 close, 9 trading sessions after the Sep 4 anchor of ~4.78-4.79% (Labor Day removes Sep 7). At this horizon the yield is close to a random walk, so the reference class does the work: 9-trading-day DGS10 changes over the trailing year have median +1.5bp and SD 9.9bp, giving a base-rate median of ~4.79. I held the median at 4.78 rather than adding drift: the upward regime (4.30 in March to 4.79 now) and 82% of Reuters-polled strategists flagging upside risk push one way, while dovish Waller/Williams remarks, a 3-year-high level, and the sell-side 3-month median of 4.50% push the other. The window is far more eventful than the average one - August CPI on Sep 11 (consensus +0.3% m/m, 2.9% y/y headline, 3.1% core, with some looking for 0.4%) and a genuinely live FOMC on Sep 16 with dots - so I widened the 10-90 from the realized 25bp to 35bp. Main counterargument: a hike is already largely priced in the front end (2Y at 4.42%, highest since Jan-2025), so a delivered-and-priced hike could leave the 10Y nearly unchanged and my width may be generous. No tradeable market price was obtainable (Kalshi 429 / empty API; no Polymarket or Manifold contract), so there is no crowd blend here. Escape mass: 5.255 is +47bp (~3.5 SD) - possible only on a hot CPI plus hawkish dots plus a term-premium/supply scare, priced at 0.6%; 3.495 is a 128bp collapse in 9 sessions with no credible mechanism, so no lower escape declared.

calls.reconciliation: Runs converged on median (4.78/4.79/4.79) and width (0.35/0.40/0.40); the real work was auditing the anchor, the dispersion class, and the escape. (1) FACTUAL - anchor: FRED DGS10 Sep 3 = 4.77 conflicts with market Sep 4 = 4.79 (TradingEconomics) / 4.784 (CNBC). Settled by instrument definition rather than a fresh fetch: the 20:00Z resolution is the 4pm ET market close, not the ~3:00-3:30pm CMT strike, and the FRED value is also one day stale, so 4.79 is the correct carry-forward. Residual 1-2bp is immaterial against a 38bp width. (2) FACTUAL - dispersion class: Run 1's calm-August SD (5-6bp over 10 sessions) is not a rival to Run 2's trailing-year 9.9bp; Run 3 notes the Jul-Sep realized regime contained no FOMC decision day, which is exactly the condition that makes it unrepresentative here. I adopt the trailing-year class widened for the CPI+FOMC-with-dots condition and confirmed by MOVE-implied ~14.5bp. I carry Run 1's and Run 3's 0.40 essentially forward at 0.38-0.39; Run 2's 0.35 is the outlier and I do not follow it, because its own stated reason for narrowness (the hike is pre-priced) affects the mean, not the variance, and a live dot plot adds variance regardless of which way the decision goes. (3) FACTUAL - market check: all three independently hit HTTP 429 on Kalshi KXTNOTEW/KXUST10AD and found no Polymarket/Manifold contract; harness title search agrees. Recorded as 'no market found'; Kalshi's year-end brackets are a near-miss contract (wrong horizon) and were not used as an anchor. (5) JUDGMENT - escape mass, the one place I depart from the pool's centre: Run 2's 0.6% treats +46bp as a clean 3-sigma Gaussian tail, but Run 1 supplies a dated 9-session precedent (Oct 2023, +45bp) in a term-premium selloff, and the current regime carries the same markers (30Y 19-year high, debt/supply concerns, an active Hormuz shipping conflict). Yield-change tails are fatter than normal; I price 1.2%, above two of three runs. I could not settle the Sep 4 DGS10 value from FRED itself or obtain any Kalshi price - no web access this run - so both carry their real uncertainty rather than being resolved by fiat.

disagreements.verdict: Unbroken tie against mean-reversion evidence (Reuters 3-mo median 4.50%, dovish Waller/Williams, expanded Treasury long-end buybacks from Sep 9, 3-year-high level). Median held at spot 4.79 - the reading I would bet on, since level evidence is already in the price.

disagreements.verdict: Rejected. Pre-pricing shifts the conditional mean, not the variance; a fresh dot plot plus the decisive August CPI adds two-sided event variance either way. Settled at 0.38.
